# Submission conversations and public moderator comments

Every community submission has a private, append-only conversation accessible only to its author and verified active site moderators. Members reply from My suggestions; moderators open the same conversation from Review queue, the save/approval receipt, or the public board's moderator-only shortcut. Replies retain their role, timestamp and wording version. Decision replies are captured automatically, including when an older client submits a moderation decision. Wording snapshots and decisions appear in the same paginated history, newest first by default with oldest-first available.

The last currently saved legacy moderator reply is preserved privately as an imported snapshot. Its original send time is not invented. Older replies overwritten before this migration cannot be reconstructed. Existing wording snapshots and audit decisions are retained. No private reply, historical wording or account identifier is projected to the public board.

Public moderator comments use a separate composer, explicit confirmation, and a server-checked public flag. Approve first, then choose Conversation & public comments -> Add a public moderator comment. The board displays up to three latest comments alongside the entry, with access to remaining pages. Only current, approved wording receives public comments. Editing, withdrawing or unpublishing an entry hides its comments publicly; old-version comments remain in private history. Moderators can hide a public comment without deleting its private audit trail. There is no conversion of a private reply into a public one.

A member reply to a clarification request returns it to the pending queue. Replies do not consume the three-new-submissions quota or change the wording version, votes, or approved text. Existing authentication, moderator quota exemption, ownership enforcement and rapid-request throttle remain. Messages do not send emails. Refresh conversation/board retrieves changes; this is not live chat or an email notification system.

Migration is additive: a protected private table, an audit capture trigger, guarded RPC, and restricted public comment projection. Client request IDs prevent duplicate replies after lost responses. Requests validate live account/session access; public reads allow only explicitly public comments on visible approved versions. No raw message-table access, role assignment, new account or service key is exposed.

Tests use disposable localhost PostgreSQL and synthetic browser accounts. Do not run reset fixtures against production. Hosted acceptance uses a rolled-back transaction. The release waits for the hosted migration before publishing its UI. Existing Auth, email settings, registration, reviewed bug evidence and nightly collector are not altered. Roll back UI asset references if needed; preserve conversations and do not drop tables.
